Questions.question: Where was Sajid when his mistake happened?
What caused Sajid to plug the cables incorrectly?
Questions.answer: He looked at the port numbers too quickly.
options: He followed an old network diagram.
He looked at the port numbers too quickly.

Questions.question: Where was Malar during her mistake?
Why did Malar’s laptops fail the update?
Questions.answer: She didn’t check the battery levels.
options: She used the wrong operating system.
She didn’t check the battery levels.

activity_c.text: Sajid and Malar walked up to Ms. Roshni after the morning lab briefing.
Both looked a bit uneasy, and Sajid spoke first.
Good morning, Madam, we need to talk to you.
We realised we made a few mistakes last week, and we want to explain them properly.
Good morning, both of you. Thank you for being honest.
Let’s go through them one by one.
Now tell me Sajid, what happened?
I plugged the cables into the wrong port.
Where exactly were you when your problem occurred?
I was near the network rack, right beside the patch-panel tray.
And when did it happen? What time was it?
It was Tuesday, around eleven fifteen, just before the connectivity test.
Alright. Now tell me—how did you end up plugging the cables into the wrong ports?
Madam… I glanced at the numbering too quickly.
I should have checked the network map first, but I didn’t.
I usually check the map, but not every day—maybe two or three times a week.
And why didn’t you check it that morning?
Honestly, madam, I thought the layout was still the same from yesterday.
But now I know I shouldn’t assume that.
Good. So how will you make sure this doesn’t happen again?
I’m going to verify the network map every morning, label the cables clearly, and double-check each port before plugging in.
Alright. Now, Malar, where were you when your mistake happened?
I was near the diagnostics desk, right beside the laptop-testing station.
And when was that?
Thursday around 2.30 p.m., during the system-update round.
And how did your laptops end up failing the update?
Madam, I selected the right update, but I didn’t check the battery levels.
Two laptops were below 10%, and they shut down halfway.
I also used the older USB installer, and the files weren’t fully verified.
Why didn’t you check the installer?
I was rushing, madam.
I check it most of the time, but that day I hurried because another batch of devices was waiting.
So how will you avoid these problems next time?
I’m going to verify the installer files, check the battery levels first, and connect each laptop to the power line before updating.
I’ll also take my time with the verification step.
Good. These are small mistakes—not disasters—but they matter.
Let’s improve our consistency this week.
